rv.q: Not only the young writer but also, it would seem, Sherman himself is dismayed by Liberace’s willingness to lie on oath, denying his sexuality just as he would deny the HIV diagnosis at the end of his life. But the more the writer obsesses about that lie, the less Liberace’s court-room denial seems to be the issue.
Fee is a good foil for him, bristling with righteous indignation that eventually crumples, and Sherman himself appears to play the writer’s older self (Can you see what they’ve done there?).
